title: The Healing of Chrestē
english: A certain widow named Chrestē was being distressed by a wild spirit, terribly cutting herself, though she was of noble birth.
She intended to travel toward the sunrise the following day; having heard about those who had been healed by Jesus, she resolved to go during that night.
The holy Longinus appeared to her, standing outside of his head.
When she asked, "Who has come here?" the holy Longinus said to her, "Do you wish to be healed?"

She replied, "Yes, Lord, this is my desire." The holy man said to her, "Go to Jerusalem, find the house of Lucius the governor, and seek the head of Longinus the centurion. Bring it to my body, and you shall be saved.
For I am Longinus, the one who tends the sheep by the roadside, and I have not found rest in the place where I was buried until now; but do this, and you shall be healed in the name of Jesus Christ.
Not only will you be healed, but I will also recruit your son, for I am the one speaking to you from outside of the head."

Upon hearing these things, the woman arranged and organized her affairs with her friends. She set out on the road, and having reached the monument, she cried out with a great voice, saying, "Lord, who is in this place, just as you revealed to me in the vision, I am coming, so help me!"
Immediately the place was shaken, and a voice came to her, saying, "Go, for the Christ is the one helping you." Having heard this voice, she traveled her entire way in joy.
When she arrived in Jerusalem, she learned from the people of the city where the house of the governor was, where they were seeking the head of the holy Longinus.
And the governor gave her a sum of honor consisting of two hundred silver denarii.
Having received this, the woman prayed and glorified God for the completion, as though she were being made worthy of the grace of God.
After receiving the head of the honored Longinus along with her son Christos, she prepared to depart in the evening.
And behold, three angels appeared to her, whose glory she was unable to behold; they held white candles in their hands and went before her, singing a hymn to God throughout the entire night.
When the dawn was breaking, they rested in the place where they had arrived to take their food.

After three days, she brought the head of the honored Longinus to his village, having traveled there with her son Christos, and she sent it to the place where he was lying at the sixth hour of the night.
Thus they arrived at the house which the Christ-loving ones had built, a place worthy of the martyr, and immediately the door opened automatically for them, and they saw the tomb...

title: Resurrection of the Youth
english: As the door opened, a light shone throughout the house. The youth entered the tomb with myrrh and aromatics and placed his head with the body. After he exited the tomb, the area was immediately secured. They returned home, rejoicing and glorifying God.

On the second night, the holy Longinus appeared to the pious woman, expressing his gratitude for the return of his head and promising that she would be healed from that day. He asked if her son would serve in the heavenly or earthly army, and she requested that he enlist her son in the heavenly army.

The next day, the youth went to the vineyard to tend to the vine. While working until the fifth hour, the holy Longinus appeared to him, asking if he was willing to serve in the name of Christ. The youth, seeing him as lightning, asked who he was, and Longinus replied that he was the one who had received his head through the youth's mother and now desired to offer the youth to God. The youth responded, 'If this is true, let it be done to me according to your word,' and immediately gave up his spirit.

The mother of the deceased, following her usual routine, had taken some food and was on her way to visit her son in the vineyard. When she arrived, she found him dead. Overcome with grief, she fell to the ground, becoming fainthearted and tearing her tunic, and lay there as if lifeless.

An angel came and strengthened her, asking why she was weeping. She replied that her only son had perished, the fruit of her womb plucked before its time. The angel reassured her, saying that her son was not lost, but was in the care of Jesus Christ. The angel instructed her to go to the village, gather some pious men, and have them carry her son's body to bury it in the tomb where the most faithful Longinus lies, and that after three days she would see her son in the heavenly army.

title: The Vision of the Mother and Longinus
english: The angel immediately came to the village, bringing comfort to the mother, and through this encounter, the villagers learned what had taken place.
She then reported everything that had happened to the villagers, and after hearing her account, they went to the bishop of Tyana and informed him of the events that had occurred.
Bishop Paphnutius, accompanied by some pious men, went to the place where the young man had died and gave permission for the mother to be summoned.

When the mother arrived, the bishop said to her, 'Do not weep over this; for he himself, having obtained the heavenly kingdom, presides much on our behalf. Let us therefore rejoice all the more and let us not be gloomy.'
Having said these things, he commanded that the body of the young man be lifted and placed with the holy Longinus, and they offered an acceptable sacrifice to the heavenly God.
The pious woman became a deacon and minister of the glorious faith; having offered many things and given much counsel, she continued in the city with the bishop.
And when midnight had come and the night had advanced, at the fourth hour of the night, there appeared to her the holy Longinus, saying: 'Why do you blaspheme me?'
And she, having been frightened and become trembling, said: 'Who are you, Lord?'
And he said to her: 'I am Longinus, the one who had campaigned against your son.'
And the woman, being perplexed about her son, crying out, said: 'Lord, if you had campaigned against him, you would not have killed him.'
And the most faithful Longinus said to her: 'See, even now you speak blasphemy. But arise and go out from your house, and you will see your son, that he has campaigned.'
Having taken hold of her hand, he brought her out, and he saw the heavens opened and a great light in the night.
And having looked up, she saw how, in ecstasy, the heavenly king and her son were advancing forward.
And the holy Longinus said to her: 'Even if now you have seen your son, that he has been arrayed for battle, have you now believed?'
And she said: 'Yes, Lord, it is enough for me what indeed I have spoken concerning you, Master.'
And immediately she became invisible.

She was, however, occupying herself night and day in the holy house, continuing in prayers and hymns and alms, and performing healings through the calling upon of Christ and of the holy martyr, glorifying God in her days for all the good things that had happened to her.

And she departed in the days of Paphnutius, bishop; and they laid her near the holy Longinus in the same house [...] to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, to whom be glory and power unto the ages of ages. Amen.
